editorial:
Imagine moving to a tiny, quiet town where everyone knows everyone, only to find out that the local charm hides some very dark secrets. You will meet Larry Flane, a man who seems to fit right into the town of Grange, but things quickly get weird. The movie has a slow-burn feel that keeps you guessing about what is actually going on. It is less about big explosions and more about the strange tension between people in a place that feels too small for its own good. You will feel like you are right there in the middle of the mystery, wondering if you can trust anyone.

The acting is solid and makes the strange plot feel grounded, though the pacing might feel a bit slow if you are used to big blockbusters. If you enjoy stories that build up to a big reveal, you will love this one. It is a great pick for a rainy weekend when you just want to get lost in a moody story. You can grab a rental on Apple TV to see it tonight, or if you really like the look of the film, adding the 4K Blu-ray to your physical collection is the way to go for the best picture quality.
endingExplained: The story wraps up when the truth about Larry comes out. You find out that his move to Grange was not an accident, but part of a larger plan involving revenge and hidden identities. The final scenes show the townspeople facing the consequences of their past lies. It ends with a sharp twist that shows Larry was always three steps ahead of everyone else, leaving you to think about how a change of scenery can change a person.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves slow mysteries and character studies.
